content:
- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (<0.4) — model is overly optimistic or fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in subsequent periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days after true price peaks, especially when sentiment is rising.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model fails to adjust forecast slope — overfits to recent highs/lows.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves when sentiment drops below 0.3 — fails to recognize risk-off behavior.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in early 30d window — model is overly confident in short-term momentum.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often overestimates the rate of increase — fails to account for regulatory or policy shocks.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment decay in the final 5–7 days of forecast horizon — underestimates correction or reversal.
